Этот собственный потолок тоже перестал быть молчаливым: когда он исчерпан, выпускается ТОТ ЖЕ toolloop.limit_reached (RN-166), потому что это тот же факт, и читающему журнал событий не нужно второе имя для него. Регидратация (диалоговый агент) — как процесс диалогового агента восстанавливает свою историю из журнала событий, когда поднимается над сессией, в которой уже есть разговор (перезапуск или PO, принимающий работу от Criativo). Один путь для всех семи, Engine.Agents.Reidratacao (RN-580): он читает хвост (последние 200 событий, а не первые), возвращает структурированные вопросы и собственные вызовы инструментов агента, а когда разговор не помещается, начинает с системного сообщения, сообщающего, сколько более ранних событий было опущено. Хэндофф — явная передача работы от одного агента другому. Явная, потому что адресат и причина записываются в журнал событий, вместо того чтобы один агент неявно «перехватывал» контекст другого. Артефакт — структурированный, валидированный результат агента. Двенадцать закрытых схем (note, business_rule, product_brief, decision_record, plano_de_teste, prototipo_navegavel, threat_model, task_blocked, qa_verdict, secops_verdict, infra_delegation_files): отсутствующее поле проваливает выпуск. Так вердикт гейта становится данными, а не текстом. business_rule проваливается и по второй причине: заголовок, уже зарегистрированный в проекте (RN-080) — поскольку артефакт является неизменяемым событием, выпуск — единственный момент, когда дубликат можно отклонить. Worktree — git worktree: рабочая копия, изолированная для каждого dev agent, над одним и тем же репозиторием. Два разработчика работают с разными ветками, не мешая друг другу. Он на агента, а не на задачу: кто берёт следующую задачу, заменяет каталог, и именно это вынуждает агента удерживать его, пока гейту ещё нужно его читать. Режим workspace — где код проекта живёт на диске, выбирается при создании и затем замораживается (ADR 0072, RN-169). container — управляемая папка под PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT, значение по умолчанию и обычное поведение; local — собственный абсолютный путь пользователя, который работает, только если он смонтирован в контейнер. Не путайте с workspace из IAM (группировка проектов и участников): одно слово для разных вещей, а режим касается диска. Состояния dev agent — working (реализует), awaiting_approval (предложил commit/push/PR, и одно из них ждёт одобрения — ни один гейт не открывается без PR, RN-050), awaiting_gate (PR открыт, ждёт вердикта), idle (нет задачи для взятия, процесс жив) и idle_tripped (сработал circuit breaker, выход только через явное перевзведение — RN-047). Первые три удерживают worktree. idle охватывает три разные причины, намеренно: очередь была пуста, взятие не удалось и — начиная с RN-502 — у проекта нет контейнера, ЗАРЕГИСТРИРОВАННОГО как running, что останавливает взятие до того, как оно произойдёт. Для последней нет четвёртого статуса: idle — единственное состояние, из которого wake ещё спасает, и каждый guard в handle_info/2 привязан к нему. Различает три причины СОБЫТИЕ (dev.idle, dev.error, dev.blocked_by_container), которое долговечно, а не статус.
documents.s: Агенты

documents.t: proposed_action — каждое действие с внешним эффектом (команда терминала, commit, push, PR, merge, расход) рождается здесь и никогда не выполняется напрямую. Двадцать один тип. Шесть состояний (RN-003). permissions.json — файл политики проекта. Сопоставляет шаблон команды (структурно, не по подстроке) и возвращает allow, deny или require_approval. deny побеждает allow — правило, проходящее через всю систему. Решение оценивает IAM → agent_autonomy → permissions.json, и deny на любом этапе возвращается немедленно (RN-004). Потолок — понижение, применяемое после всей политики, выше которого никакая конфигурация не может поднять. Их два: merge в защищённую ветку (RN-006) и патч инструкции (RN-007). Потолок — это разница между «нет по умолчанию» и «нет». agent_autonomy — режим работы агента в проекте: manual (каждое действие запрашивает одобрение) или автоматический. Это первый переключатель, который нужно перевести при инциденте со стоимостью. Защищённая ветка — dev, qa, rc, main. Merge в любую из них — всегда решение человека. Эквивалентная защита на платформе (GitHub/GitLab) различается между провайдерами и не является гейтом — гейт это домен (ADR 0028).
documents.s: Одобрение

documents.t: Гейт — обязательный шлюз между PR разработчика и merge. Их два: QA (семантический, запускает LLM) и SecOps (детерминированный, запускает сканер). Порядок неизменен: awaiting_qa → awaiting_secops → awaiting_user (RN-014). awaiting_user — терминальное состояние машины гейтов. Терминальное намеренно: система никогда не делает merge сама. changes_requested — гейт, возвращающий работу разработчику, в той же ветке. Новый PR не открывается. Цикл K — потолок исправлений на задачу. Каждый возврат расходует один раунд; когда они исчерпаны, задача блокируется с причиной вместо бесконечного вращения. Субагент наследует потолок базового агента (RN-015). task_blocked — артефакт, выпускаемый, когда задача застревает: несёт reason и diagnosis. Это читаемая запись о сбое, а не молчание. Припаркованный цикл гейта — цикл QA/SecOps, оставшийся in_progress без активности более 2 часов. GateRescuer больше не возобновляет его сам (при загрузке или по своему тику): он записывает gate.rescue_parked и устанавливает parked_at, и возобновить его может только жест человека — сегодня GateRescuer.retomar_estacionado/3 через bin/engine rpc оператора (ADR 0207, RN-722). Цикл, у сессии которого есть одобрение, ожидающее от актора гейта, тоже не перезапускается: он ждёт вас. НЕДАВНИЙ цикл in_progress, который убил сам перезапуск engine, не паркуется и не ждёт 15-минутного порога: при загрузке, если ни один узел кластера не держит его в работе, rescuer записывает gate.interrupted и сразу перезапускает его (RN-823). Гейт implementavel (реализуемость) — шлюз ДО разработки, до появления dev agent или worktree: Dev Lead оценивает, реализуема ли история, исходя из самой истории и текущего module_map (до ADR 0192 входом был план тестирования QA-стратегии). dono: dev-lead, aprovacao_humana: true, severidade: warn (ADR 0090). QA-стратегия — qa-lead во втором МОМЕНТЕ (тот же процесс, результат, отдельный от вердикта PR): он создаёт план тестирования (синтез, исполняемые критерии, стратегия автоматизации) для ПОСТАВКИ ОДНОЙ задачи, ПОСЛЕ того как dev agent её выполнил, — первый шаг проверки qa-verificada, как вход для неё, никогда не собственный вердикт (RN-674, ADR 0192). Никогда не приостанавливается — ни один из его инструментов не проходит через конвейер действий. AppSec — secops во втором МОМЕНТЕ, та же форма, что у QA-стратегии над qa-lead: ТОТ ЖЕ процесс (SecOpsAgentServer.run_design/2) создаёт модель угроз STRIDE-lite по ДИЗАЙНУ истории — без worktree, без task_id, до появления какого-либо кода или PR. Он никогда ничего не одобряет и не отклоняет; он завершается выпуском artifact.threat_model и передаёт его Arquiteto, Dev Lead и Infra. Запускается assess_implementability от Dev Lead, параллельно, один раз на историю (RN-360, RN-539, ADR 0090).
documents.s: Гейты и выполнение

documents.t: Бизнес-правило (RN) — единица, выпускаемая Criativo и привязанная к историям. Правило без истории — это пробел в покрытии, а не ошибка (RN-011). История — четыре состояния; выход из draft требует DoD, DoR, как минимум одного функционального требования и как минимум одного связанного правила (RN-010). DoD / DoR — Definition of Done и Definition of Ready. Здесь это не церемония: без обоих история не меняет состояние. module_map — карта модулей системы от Arquiteto. Определяет, сколько существует dev agent (по одному на модуль) и к какому модулю относится каждая история. Не может содержать цикл (RN-013); удалённый модуль понижает истории, которые от него зависели (RN-012). Образ проекта (artifact.project_image) — решение Arquiteto о том, какой контейнер запускает код проекта: OCI-образ (обязателен явный тег, latest отклоняется), сетевой режим (none по умолчанию, egress разрешён) и потолок ресурсов. Версионируется в журнале событий, как module_map. Пока его нет, состояние sem_decisao (нет решения) держит вкладку Code закрытой (RN-105).
documents.s: Бэклог и архитектура

documents.t: Учёт потребления (metering) — запись потребления по каждому вызову в token_usage: токены, стоимость в микроединицах, задержка, модель, агент. Это запись, а не возврат средств. Бюджет — потолок расходов с исключительной областью: проект или сессия, никогда оба (RN-017). Уведомляет на 70/90/100% без повторов. policy — поведение бюджета на потолке: block отклоняет вызов, allow только записывает его. Проект с allow не останавливается сам — это самая частая причина «бюджет не удержал» (RN-019). Binding — связь между областью и моделью LLM. Разрешается каскадом: сессия > агент > область > проект > workspace, первое существующее (RN-020). Поэтому можно поставить дорогую модель только на QA. area — это значение ПО УМОЛЧАНИЮ, общее для lead и его субагентов, и агент может от него отличаться (RN-102). Грань capability — то, что провайдер объявляет о модели: читает изображения, генерирует изображения, делает thinking, принимает tools. Приходит из удалённого каталога при синхронизации; false означает «не объявил», а никогда не «не умеет» (RN-056). Использование модели — для чего этот workspace использует модель (codigo, documentacao, analise, imagem, conversa). Это мнение оператора, а не capability: ни один каталог не публикует «хороша для кода». Пометка использования не включает модель в селекторе (RN-057).
documents.s: Стоимость

documents.t: Гипотеза — результат Psicólogo: утверждение о команде с evidenceEventIds, указывающими на реальные события анализируемой сессии. Без действительных доказательств она не записывается (RN-021). Причина завершения — детерминированная классификация того, почему что-то сломалось: infra, modelo, código или política. Берётся из записанной причины, никогда из суждения LLM и никогда методом исключения (RN-023). proficiency_profile — профиль компетенций пользователя, поддерживаемый Anamnese, по каждой компетенции. Шесть процессных компетенций, закрытый список (git, agile, arquitetura, testes, seguranca, infra), плюс технические стеки, выведенные из module_map. Ничто вне каталога не имеет пути записи (RN-024) — Anamnese профилирует техническую компетенцию, а не человека. Допустимый субъект — кого может профилировать раунд Anamnese: ДЕЙСТВУЮЩИЙ участник проекта (строка проекта, а иначе — workspace), вне opt-out, с СОБСТВЕННЫМ взаимодействием в окне. Если никого нет, раунд не вызывает LLM (RN-680). Факт профиля (FatoDoPerfil) — гипотеза Psicólogo, которую ПРИНЯЛ человек, которому принадлежит сессия, спроецированная в граф из psychologist.hypothesis_accepted и передаваемая агентам, разговаривающим с этим человеком, как эфемерное системное сообщение (RN-680). instruction_patch — версионированное предложение изменить инструкцию агента. Никогда не одобряется автоматически (RN-007); отклонённое не предлагается повторно (RN-026); откат создаёт новую версию вместо удаления (RN-027).
documents.s: Psicólogo и Anamnese

documents.t: GitProvider — нормализованный контракт из двенадцати операций, который реализуют Local, GitHub и GitLab. Единый набор контрактных тестов запускается против всех трёх. Capability — объявление того, что поддерживает данный провайдер. Неподдерживаемая операция отклоняется с явной ошибкой, никогда не молчаливым сбоем (RN-028). Bootstrap Gitflow — шесть шагов, подготавливающих репозиторий (постоянные ветки, защиты, базовые файлы). Идемпотентный и возобновляемый: skip — это успех (RN-029). Envelope encryption — каждый секрет пользователя шифруется собственным DEK (data encryption key), а DEK «оборачивается» ключом CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY. Ротация мастер-ключа переоборачивает DEK, не трогая шифротекст, — поэтому ротацию можно прерывать (runbook). wrapped_dek — обёрнутый DEK в том виде, в каком он хранится в базе. Не указывает, каким ключом он обёрнут — именно это свойство делает ротацию процедурой из трёх шагов, а не заменой переменной.
documents.s: Git и секреты

documents.t: Oban — библиотека очередей Elixir, использующая Postgres как бэкенд. Глубина очереди (oban_queue_depth) — метрика, управляющая HPA engine. Drain — фаза preStop engine: /ready начинает отвечать 503, новые сессии отклоняются, и каждая сессия на узле предлагается живому соседу. То, что не принято, закрывается как closed_abnormally / node_shutdown — корректное завершение, а не сирота. Принятие (adoption) — другой узел берёт на себя процесс сессии. Происходит во время drain (активная передача) и в SessionAdoptionWorker, который проходит каждые 30 с, чтобы покрыть kill -9 и OOMKill, когда preStop не выполняется. :global — распределённый реестр Erlang. Гарантирует одного владельца на сессию во всём кластере; без сформированного кластера Erlang каждая реплика становится островом (ADR 0026). Корневой trace — одна сессия = один trace, охватывающий api ↔ engine. traceparent сохраняется в sessions.trace_parent, и именно его используют для навигации в Tempo. trace_id рождается в web (браузер генерирует traceparent) и существует даже без коллектора: экспорт — решение, отдельное от инструментирования (ADR 0035). Путь через слои — последовательность границ, которые запрос пересекает в api (interfaces → application → infrastructure), с длительностью каждого шага, выдаваемая одной строкой лога на запрос. Она берётся из AsyncLocalStorage, наполняемого декоратором @Traced, а не из span — именно это позволяет ей работать без коллектора. См. наблюдаемость. Слой — в пути выше, метка границы: interfaces, application, domain или infrastructure. Соответствует каталогам под apps/api/src/ и правилу зависимостей между ними.
documents.s: Инфраструктура

documents.t: An artifact is the structured and validated output of an agent. Concretely: an artifact.<type> event in the log, with the payload validated against a closed schema before being written. There is no artifact table. Validation happens in one place only — Engine.Harness.ArtifactSchemas — and a missing required field fails the emission, instead of writing a half-formed artifact.
documents.s: Artifacts

documents.t: This is the most important distinction on this page, and it's easy to miss: origin meaning tool the model decides to emit, calling emit_artifact server the code emits when the outcome happens; the model doesn't choose Only three types are emittable by tool: note, business_rule and decision_record. Everything else is emitted by the server. The reason is the same in every case: when the artifact is the record of an outcome, letting the model choose whether to emit it means letting it omit it. A DevAgent that gives up shouldn't be able to decide not to record that it gave up. The session type filters no artifact. RN-097 gave the session a kind (consultiva | criativa) and put a guard on event append, but it reaches one type — execution.activated — and no artifact is it. A consultative session records artifact.business_rule all the same: what it doesn't do is enter execution. Whoever arrives at the type rule tends to assume the opposite, and the wrong assumption here would erase the record of an entire conversation. The session STATE filters by actor. Since RN-581 a closed/closed_abnormally session refuses conversation with a 409, and "conversation" includes any event whose actor is a conversational agent — so an artifact.* from the Creative agent, the PO, the Architect, the Dev Lead, the UX Designer, the Staff or the Infra Lead no longer lands in a closed session, while the same artifact types emitted by the Psychologist, which runs on the closed session, still do. The type never decides; the actor does.
documents.s: Who can emit what

documents.t: field required title ✅ body ✅
documents.s: note — tool

documents.t: field required title ✅ description ✅ origin ✅ — non-empty list origin references the conversation events that originated the rule. An empty list fails: it is the traceability of the rule back to where it was stated, and without it the rule becomes an assertion with no provenance. :::caution The model needs to KNOW the field names The description of the emit_artifact tool is generated from these schemas (ArtifactSchemas.required/1) and names each required field, in English, with a filled-in example. This isn't fussiness: the previous description simply said "emits a typed artifact" and listed the types. In a real execution the model — conversing in Portuguese — guessed titulo/descricao/comportamento, and the four business rules from that conversation were silently rejected. origin as free text also fails: it has to be a list, and the description says so in plain terms (RN-061). :::
documents.s: business_rule — tool

documents.t: field required context ✅ options ✅ — list choice ✅ consequences ✅ The "summarized ADR" any of the six conversational agents can emit — the Creative, PO, Architect, Dev Lead, UX Designer and Staff all carry emit_artifact with this type (RN-505). No cross-field validation on purpose: choice doesn't have to match one of the options verbatim — free text is more robust, and the generic schema only checks key presence, the same rule as note/business_rule. It reuses the generic pattern instead of the dedicated one (artifact.project_image/artifact.c4_diagram, versioned, own TS schema, own HTTP route): a decision is append-only by nature, not a "current" value that gets replaced. It is deliberately distinct from open_adr_pr (Architect-only, commits a real file under docs/adr/*.md and opens a real PR with mandatory human approval) — the two coexist for different scales of decision: decision_record is frictionless, searchable in the session log, for any relevant decision; open_adr_pr is for when the decision is big enough to become a real repository document.
documents.s: decision_record — tool

documents.t: field required questionId ✅ — uuid, generated by the tool pergunta ✅ — up to 500 characters afeta ✅ — {regras, historias, tarefas}, lists of ids sugestao optional — up to 300 characters A doubt an agent leaves for the user (ADR 0214, RN-862). It is not emittable by emit_artifact: only the Creative, PO, Architect and Dev Lead emit it, through their own declare_open_question tool, which also records autor and sessionId. The api closes it with open_question.answered.
documents.s: open_question — own tool

documents.t: field required title ✅ summary ✅ rules ✅ Validatable, but not emittable by tool. The Creative server emits it only after you confirm readiness — never through a model tool call. Since ADR 0185 the click that asks for it — "I'm ready — the need is validated" — also records necessity.validated with productBriefId: null: the brief is the next product_brief after that readiness.confirmed, and the handoff that carries it to the PO is accepted on behalf of whoever clicked (RN-657, RN-658).
documents.s: product_brief — server

documents.t: field required taskId ✅ agentId ✅ reason ✅ diagnosis ✅ Emitted when the DevAgent gives up on the task: a suite that doesn't close, an iteration ceiling, a blown budget, or a stall without signaling. It is the record of the outcome.
documents.s: task_blocked — server

documents.t: field required veredito ✅ — approved, changes_requested or needs_user_decision (RN-862), nothing else resumo ✅ itens ✅ taskId or prActionId ✅ — exactly one coverageMatrix optional, QA only Three extra validations live here: The verdict is closed to the same two values as the api's gate state machine. A value outside that would make the use case blow up further down the line — rejecting the artifact at emission is the right place to fail. The subject is exclusive. A verdict is about one dev task (taskId) or about one infra PR (prActionId) — never both, never neither. Same artifact type, different consumers. coverageMatrix is optional on purpose. A QA verdict without a coverage matrix is still a valid verdict; losing it entirely because of one missing field would be worse than recording it incomplete. SecOps is deterministic — it has no LLM. The QA verdict is born from the emit_qa_verdict tool, which is enforced separately. In neither case does the model choose to emit.
documents.s: qa_verdict and secops_verdict — server

documents.t: field required files ✅ — non-empty list summary ✅ Result of ONE delegate from the Infra area (Phase 8c, ADR 0038) — the lead itself (Dockerfiles/compose) or the Workflows subagent (CI pipeline). The InfraLeadServer emits this after each delegate finishes, just to have a parecer_artifact_id to reference in the delegations table — never seen from outside the area. What the api sees is the consolidated PR, via open_infra_pr (the same mechanism as always, untouched by Phase 8c). An empty files fails for the same reason as nada_a_validar/1 in InfraGateRunner (ADR 0021): a delegate with no files at all didn't finish anything, and "empty" should never pass as "done".
documents.s: infra_delegation_files — server

documents.t: field required personas ✅ — non-empty list jornadas ✅ — non-empty list prototipo ✅ — telas non-empty resumo ✅ The prototype the UX Designer produces (ADR 0087), from the Creative's necessidade-de-negocio. It is not note/business_rule — the UX Designer emits via propose_prototype, a DEDICATED tool (Engine.Agents.UxDesignerTools), and this module only validates the SHAPE, the same mechanism as product_brief: validatable here without being on the list of types emittable via emit_artifact. Empty personas/jornadas, or a prototipo with no screen at all, fail by the same rule as business_rule.origin (line 59): an artifact with no content isn't worth recording. A successful propose_prototype ends the turn (the same reasoning as propose_execution_plan/propose_infra_pr) — no proposed_action, no suspension: proposing a prototype has no external effect.
documents.s: prototipo_navegavel — tool (propose_prototype, not emit_artifact)

documents.t: field required storyId ✅ taskId ✅ — since ADR 0192 planoDeTeste ✅ criteriosExecutaveis ✅ — non-empty list estrategiaDeAutomacao ✅ The deliverable of QA-strategy (ADR 0090; docs/fluxo.yml, role qa-estrategia, the qa-lead's second moment). Since ADR 0192 (RN-674) it is the test plan for ONE task's DELIVERY, written AFTER the dev agent delivered, over the dev's worktree and the files the delivery touched: it is the first step of the qa-verificada cycle (QaLeadServer.run_area/3), consumed as INPUT by the Automation subspecialty, and found again by taskId on the correction round. Until ADR 0192 it was emitted PRE-DEV and fed the implementavel gate. It is born from emit_plano_de_teste, but the model doesn't emit the artifact directly — Engine.Gates.QaEstrategiaAgent extracts the result from the tool call and calls ArtifactEmitter.emit/5, the same pattern as qa_verdict/task_blocked. An empty criteriosExecutaveis fails for the same reason as infra_delegation_files: a plan with no criteria at all isn't a plan.
documents.s: plano_de_teste — server

documents.t: field required storyId ✅ threatModel ✅ requisitosDeSeguranca ✅ SecOps's "second moment" (RN-360, ADR 0090) — a STRIDE-lite checklist over the DESIGN of a story, before any code exists, the same second-moment pattern as qa-estrategia. Engine.Gates.SecOpsAgentServer.run_design/2 emits after Engine.Gates.AppSecAgent.run/3 (no Terminal, no Diff/Scanner/ DevAgentState) finishes the loop with emit_threat_model — the model doesn't choose to emit, the server emits when the loop ends. riscos is left out of the required fields: an empty list is a valid answer (not every story carries residual risk) and the tool already guarantees the KEY exists — there's no "forgotten" to distinguish from "none". The artifact is always recorded, but the HANDOFFS that carry it are not: since RN-636 AppSec offers it only to a target (arquiteto, dev-lead, infra) that has no pending offer and is not active in the project. The threat model of a second story stays in the log without an offer of its own — the first offer, still pending, is not replaced (ADR 0182).
documents.s: threat_model — server

documents.t: Some artifact.* event types exist in the log without being in this registry, because they are emitted by the api, not by the engine: event origin artifact.module_map the Architect, via a use case in the api — each module may carry resources (cpus, memoryMb, pidsLimit), and the Infra starts the container with their SUM (ADR 0199, RN-683) artifact.insight analysis, via a use case in the api artifact.project_image the Architect, via a use case in the api (ADR 0065, RN-105) artifact.module_routing the Architect, via a use case in the api — one candidate image per module of the current module_map; the Architect CANDIDATES, Infra ELECTS in a later step (ADR 0131, RN-487) artifact.module_contracts the Architect, via a use case in the api — per module of the current module_map, what it EXPOSES; read by dev agents through listar_contratos_de_modulos instead of another module's worktree (ADR 0200, RN-684) They have their own validations in the api's domain. The asymmetry is historical, and is noted as technical debt: ideally every artifact.* would go through a single registry.
documents.s: Artifacts that don't go through here

documents.t: error cause {:unknown_type, tipo} type outside the twelve {:missing_keys, [...]} required fields missing, all named :origem_invalida business_rule.origin empty or not a list {:sujeito_invalido, chaves} verdict with both subjects, or with neither {:veredito_invalido, valor} verdict outside approved / changes_requested / needs_user_decision :invalid_payload payload is not a map The failure goes back to the agent as the tool result. A model that emits a malformed artifact receives the error and can correct it — within the ToolLoop's iteration ceiling.
documents.s: When validation fails

documents.t: BRB-NNN findings are raised and prioritised in the maintainer's vault (07-backlog/Backlog de Melhorias (Brabo)), which holds all 33 of them with priority, effort, origin, proposal and a "done when". That register is the source for what a finding is and for whether it is closed. This file is the part the repository can verify. Created by FASE 29, session 1 (fase-29-instalacao-de-uma-linha.md).
documents.s: BRB register

documents.t: Every id from BRB-001 to BRB-033 has exactly one row, in numeric order. Until 2026-09-27 the page listed only the findings the code could prove or disprove — 11 of 33 — and the rest were invisible here, including six the vault had since measured as fixed (AT-186). A row per id costs nothing and makes the absence of evidence visible instead of silent. Each row carries: vault state — copied from the vault register as of 2026-09-27. It is the maintainer's call and is never decided here. measured here — what the repository shows, measured against dev at 34c1c83bdc on 2026-09-27 unless the evidence dates it otherwise. evidence — the file:line, PR or run behind that measurement. A finding whose subject lives outside this repository (the vault's own notes, a product decision, a paid credential) still gets a row, marked not verifiable here, with the reason. An id with no information at all would carry a TODO(humano) — none does today. A new BRB-NNN in the vault gets its row here in the same change that first mentions it.
documents.s: Coverage criterion

documents.t: BRB-018 is what the second rule below looks like in practice. When this file was born nothing about it had changed in the code — no reprojection was written — but the repository gained the ability to say why it was still open and what it cost while it was, so the row existed before the fix did. The command now exists (RN-569); the row stays because the cluster proof does not. Two ids — BRB-005 and BRB-031 — were referenced across five documents here, in prose, with no state anyone could check. The other ids were invisible to this repository entirely: a full-disk search returned only those two. The cost was measured, not imagined. Planning FASE 29 listed six BRB items as prerequisites or risks; checking each against dev found that two describe defects already fixed here, and that a third had been misread from its id alone — see BRB-004 below, which is not about the tag anyone assumes. Two rules follow: State is backed by file:line, measured, never remembered. The vault owns the finding; the repository owns the evidence. Where the two disagree about whether something still happens, the repository wins — it is the thing being described. Whether an item is formally closed stays the maintainer's call, in the vault.
documents.s: Why this file exists

documents.t: id title (from the vault) prio vault state measured here evidence BRB-001 Cap self-downgrade through the REMOVAL of a project membership P1 closed 2026-09-12 (PR #531) defect no longer reproduces RemoveProjectMemberUseCase.execute took (projectId, userId) — no actor — and the controller called it with the two route params, so a maintainer whose authority came from the project row (viewer in the workspace) could remove their own row and drop to viewer irreversibly; the case was pinned in a test whose own name said it was open. ADR 0127 had declared the gap in writing, cost estimate included. Closed by ADR 0156 / RN-556: the actor now reaches the use case, remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento delegates to the existing cap-2 rule with the workspace role as the requested one, and the lacuna test was INVERTED rather than deleted. The workspace-owner cap deliberately gets no counterpart — removal can only raise an owner BRB-002 Cap self-movement on the WORKSPACE member upsert P2 closed 2026-09-12 (PR #533) defect no longer reproduces AddWorkspaceMemberUseCase.execute took (workspaceId, userId, role) and called workspaces.addMember — no actor — while the controller (@Post(':workspaceId/members'), @RequireRole('owner')) passed the raw body with no @CurrentUser(). An owner could write themselves viewer and lose the whole workspace: nothing above catches the fall, and WorkspacesController has no member @Delete (measured), so undoing is that same route, demanding the owner just abandoned. ADR 0127 named it in writing ("same class of defect, one scope up") and ADR 0156 left it as a separate decision. Closed by ADR 0157 / RN-557: the actor reaches the use case and changing your own role is 403 in both directions. The cap does not count owners (the clause already guarantees a workspace never reaches zero, since removing the last owner would take that owner), and cap 1 gets no counterpart here — @RequireRole('owner') already forbids the hierarchy inversion it exists to stop, and adding it would make owner an absorbing state with no HTTP exit. The same ADR closes self-promotion on both association routes, revising ADR 0127's Consequences: it is the only half of the movement that escalates privilege BRB-003 Fix the three OpenAPI descriptions that promise "the higher of the two" (RN-471) P2 closed 2026-09-27 (AT-136) defect no longer reproduces grep -rn "higher of the two" apps/api/src is empty. apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/add-member.dto.ts:29 and projects.controller.ts:190,239 say the project role OVERRIDES the workspace one in both directions — the text arrived with ADR 0127 / RN-472 (PR #445). First measured 2026-09-11 (AT-017) BRB-004 Pin third-party images (neo4j, pgvector, ollama) by digest P2 open defect no longer reproduces Was: every third-party image pinned by tag, not digest. Tag pinning had closed a different gap (PRs #401/#419) and this row read as if that were the fix — the reason the id/description distinction below earns its keep. Closed by ADR 0159: all 37 third-party references go by index digest with the tag in a trailing comment, and scripts/ci/imagens-pinadas.ts fails the lint job on a mutable reference, on a digest with no tag comment, and on the same tag carrying two different digests. The count is 37 and not the finding's own list, because three whole places were outside it: the Dockerfile FROM lines (the base of the four images we publish and sign), and the services: images of ci.yml/golden-set-rag.yml — the CI runner the sibling rule already protects, reached by the other door. The five images the product publishes are deliberately not covered (four when the row was written; the fifth, the broker, came with ADR 0162): no third party can move them, brabo-api:prod is a local tag whose digest does not exist before the build, and where they cross a registry ADR 0119 already resolves them — the overlay holds a marker on purpose, so a literal there would fail the correct state. Declared and not fixed, because it is the price of the pin: a digest gets no security update until someone bumps it by hand, and Dependabot's docker ecosystem stays off — a separate decision. Also uncovered, and stated: otel-collector-values.yaml, where image: opens a map whose tag the Helm chart chooses BRB-005 Sign the GHCR images and the runner binaries P2 open implemented, not yet exercised Was: no cosign/sigstore/attestation anywhere, release.yml without id-token: write, no checksums.txt. Now: release.yml signs the five images by digest (four when written; ADR 0162 added the broker) and verifies them in the same run; build-runner-binaries.yml gained a checksums job publishing one signed manifest for the five targets (ADR 0149, RN-524); verification procedure in the runbook. Not exercised: signing only runs on a real final tag, so nothing here proves it end to end yet. Still uncovered, and a separate item: OS code-signing of the binaries (notarization/Authenticode). Session 3 made the download proxy GET /runner-releases/binary verify — but only the sha256 against the release's checksums.txt, never the manifest's signature (RN-525): that is integrity, not provenance, and whoever can rewrite the Release rewrites both files. Both ways for the api to check the signature were measured and refused: cosign in the image is 155 MB (nearly doubling an Alpine+Node runtime image), and @sigstore/verify+@sigstore/tuf is cheap (2.5 MB) but makes a @Public() route depend on a second third-party host (tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev) to verify something no Release carries yet — unprovable, and ADRs 0041/0042 forbid declaring an unproven capability. The signature consumer is install.sh (session 4/7), which has a real pinned cosign. So the provenance half of the proxy stays open, and refusal is already named there: a Release without checksums.txt is refused, not served with a warning BRB-006 Automate updating the pinned SHAs (Dependabot/Renovate) P3 open defect no longer reproduces .github/dependabot.yml:35 declares the github-actions ecosystem (and npm, :55/:61), all with target-branch: dev; .github/workflows/dependabot-para-dev.yml routes security updates to dev, and scripts/ci/dependabot-justifica-pin.ts (AT-094) writes the docs-not-needed: line on a pin-only bump. Not measured here: the "done when" asks for a real bump PR passing actions-pinadas.ts with no manual step — no PR was listed for this row BRB-007 Run the Automation-QA golden set in CI P2 delivered 2026-09-27 (PR #687, #689), not marked closed defect no longer reproduces .github/workflows/golden-set-qa.yml:39 runs it weekly (cron: '17 1 * * 6') plus workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request (ADR 0168). The instrument measures again under RN-502: the seed brings the container up through container_start (AT-076), and the proof runs scored 3/6 against a floor of 1/6. The floor in apps/engine/test/fixtures/golden_set_qa/floor.json is still the 2026-08-30 one — only a human writes it BRB-008 Change (or justify) the golden-set seed's default model P2 open still reproduces apps/api/scripts/seed-golden-set-qa.ts:119 still defaults to qwen2.5-coder:latest, whose floor in apps/engine/test/fixtures/golden_set_qa/floor.json is 1/6 (against 4/6 for gpt-oss:20b). No decision recorded BRB-009 Schedule the three property proofs (test-restore, rollout-test, hpa-test) P2 open open — scheduled now; the mutation of the restore is caught, the last good run is a workflow artifact and not yet a metric Was: the three targets (Makefile:41-48) ran only when someone typed make, and no workflow brought up a cluster (grep -rn "k3d|kind" .github/workflows/ was empty). Now .github/workflows/propriedades.yml runs weekly and on workflow_dispatch: it installs k3d/helm/kubectl by pinned checksum, runs the same deploy/k8s/bootstrap.sh a human runs, then make smoke-k8s, make hpa-test, make rollout-test and make test-restore, each timed into the run summary; a failing target opens an issue titled after it, and a repeat failure comments on the open one instead of opening another. It is not a gate and not a required check. Its first run already paid for itself: the bootstrap died creating the CNPG cluster, because the digest-only imageName ADR 0159 wrote is refused by the operator's webhook — kubeconform runs no webhook, so the manifests job had stayed green. Nine more followed, all fixed in the same change (listed in the runbook), one of them outside the local cluster: brabo-restore died on COMMENT ON EXTENSION vector on any Postgres where the app role is not a superuser. The first fully green run is 34784563928 (2026-09-13, 12 min 56 s), green again on a second attempt. The rollout proof reported an orphan session in one of four runs that reached it, and that is declared, not fixed. AT-126 closed the first of the two remaining clauses: make test-restore-mutacao breaks the restore on purpose (a table in the source that the dump does not have) and the scheduled run fails, and opens its own issue, if the restore does not reject it naming that table; a run in which the restore was deliberately blinded failed on that step. Still open, and not this repository's call to close from CI: the last successful run is now dated by the workflow (the restore-ultima-execucao-boa artifact, written only when the restore and the deliberate break both passed) but is not a metric next to the backup alerts nor a backupRuns row — that needs code in apps/api. Measured durations and cadence: runbook, Scheduled property proofs BRB-010 Exercise the CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY rotation with a script and a test P2 closed 2026-09-27 (AT-136) defect no longer reproduces Closed by PR #551, ADR 0158 / RN-562: apps/api/src/scripts/rewrap-deks.ts exports the core (reenvelopar) and apps/api/test/scripts/rewrap-deks.spec.ts is the named verification, against a real Postgres and both envelope tables; the runbook runs it (docs/runbook.md:2770). The command name differs from the finding's proposal (credenciais:reenvelopar); the "done when" — a named verification — is met. Since AT-146 the rotation also has a cluster rehearsal: it had never run in a real environment (maintainer, 2026-09-27), and make test-rotacao-chave-mestra-k8s runs the runbook's three steps weekly in propriedades.yml — the ExternalSecret, an api restart and the image's rewrap-deks.js included (first green run 36502355798) BRB-011 Cover the single point of failure of alerting (Grafana without Alertmanager) P2 open still reproduces deploy/k8s/observability/alerts/brabo-alerts.yaml:8 still says there is no Alertmanager and no receiver; nothing in deploy/k8s warns when Grafana itself stops evaluating (measured by AT-121, 2026-09-19) BRB-012 Prove the LLM providers never exercised against a real credential P3 open not verifiable here The run needs paid keys this repository does not hold. What the repository records: the chat table in docs/explanation/aceite-providers.md:108-115 (state as of 2026-08-07) has OpenRouter run for real and Together, DeepInfra, NVIDIA NIM, Bitdeer and Vultr skipped for a missing *_TEST_KEY; the embeddings table above it (:83-93) proves only Ollama BRB-013 Clean up the leftovers of the rc step (enum and protected-branch list) P3 open partly reproduces — the repository half is a decision apps/api/src/domain/actions/protected-branches.ts:12 keeps rc and apps/api/src/db/schema/git.ts:24 keeps create_rc_branch — on purpose: the list decides what the merge cap refuses, and repositories bootstrapped by older versions still have the branch (CLAUDE.md, Conventions). The other half — two vault notes still listing rc as protected — lives in the vault BRB-014 Migrate the rest of api-types.ts to generated types P3 open still reproduces apps/web/src/lib/api-types.ts is 1,852 lines with 185 exports (the finding said ~1,600), next to the generated api-types.generated.ts BRB-015 Keep decomposing SessionPage.tsx P3 open defect no longer reproduces apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx is 834 lines (was 2,637 on dev at 018b8cd24c; the finding said 2,479, under pages/), after the ten mechanical PRs of ADR 0176 (AT-138). The "done when" is under 1,000, and it is now locked: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.teto.test.ts fails the file at 1,000 lines or more, proven by mutation. Raising the ceiling takes a new ADR BRB-016 Record the key id in the wrapped_dek to simplify rotation P3 closed 2026-09-27 (AT-136) defect no longer reproduces Closed by PR #551, ADR 0158 / RN-563: key_id (the master key's fingerprint) in apps/api/src/db/schema/llm.ts:275 and git.ts:76, so "how many credentials are still on the previous key?" is one query (IS DISTINCT FROM, counting unlabelled rows as pending). The label never decides whether an envelope opens — GCM does BRB-017 Meet the GPL obligation of the tools baked into the published engine image P1 open defect no longer reproduces Was: nothing under docker/engine/ mentioned licences, an obligation that became real when ADR 0119 started publishing to GHCR on every final tag. The offer existed and was good — THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the root, naming each component, its exact version and its licence — it just did not travel. It does now: docker/engine/Dockerfile.prod:190-192 copies it to /usr/share/doc/brabo/, before the USER and as root, so it ships inside every published engine image (PR #532). Re-measured 2026-10-01 (AT-120): by the maintainer's decision the same COPY, in the same form, is in the four other production Dockerfiles (api, web, broker, backup), and the runner Release carries the file as an asset inside the signed checksums.txt — no artifact is declared exempt. Locked by scripts/ci/oferta-de-fonte-na-imagem.spec.ts (each Dockerfile's final stage, the Release asset, mutation cases), and the ci.yml image job reads the file back out of each of the five images it builds. Found on the way: the engine copy was unreadable by the image's non-root user (BuildKit applied --chmod=0644 to the directory it created), so the documented docker run … cat check failed with "Permission denied"; the directory is now created 0755 first. Two things stay open, and neither is a defect: the sidecar (path 3) is still an unmade architecture choice, and whether the obligation is met is a legal judgement this repository cannot assert — it can only say the image carries the offer. Found on the way: the document asserted the opposite of what the repository does ("no image is published today", superseded by ADR 0119), and its TODO(humano) to decide "before the first push" expired unread BRB-018 Write and test the reconstruction of the Neo4j projection from the event log P2 open implemented and proven on the local cluster (scheduled); no large-log time measurement Was: no reprojection command anywhere (grep reprojet/reproject/graph:repro across apps/ and scripts/ returned nothing), while ADR 0152 decision 4 had already refused to back up neo4j_data on the grounds that reprojection is the answer. Now: apps/api/src/scripts/reprojetar-grafo.ts (pnpm --filter api grafo:reprojetar, node scripts/reprojetar-grafo.js in the image) walks session_events and the closed sessions by cursor, in batches, and hands each source to GraphEventTranslator — the same translation the forward GraphProjector now calls, extracted from it rather than written twice (RN-569). Idempotent (MERGE, never deletes), whole log or --project, does not touch the outbox the live projector keeps its progress in, and fails named when Neo4j is down or the project does not exist. The procedure is in the runbook (Losing the graph). The proof is make test-reprojecao (apps/api/test/scripts/reprojetar-grafo.spec.ts): forward-project a scenario, wipe its subgraph, reproject, compare node and edge counts and the key list, reproject again — green against the development compose's Neo4j, and it skips where there is no Neo4j, which includes the api CI job. The cluster proof (AT-127): make test-reprojecao-k8s (deploy/k8s/test-reprojecao.sh) is the fourth target of propriedades.yml — on a project it creates (a closed session, two events) it runs node scripts/reprojetar-grafo.js --project inside the api pod, wipes that subgraph in the cluster's Neo4j, reprojects and requires the same counts (5 nodes, 4 edges), then reprojects again; green in run 35471428634 in 16 s, after two runs that failed in the script itself (35469877869, 35470685598). Since AT-191 the scenario has four events — a Psychologist hypothesis and an Anamnesis profile besides the message and the handoff — so it exercises every path of the translator, and the counts are 9 nodes and 6 edges (run 36498776825, 18 s). It does not depend on test-restore or on the other targets' state. Still not closed: there is no time measurement on a large event log (the only real run is the dev compose, 98 events, 2.5 s), and PromptTemplate/PromptVersion are not in the event log — they come back through scripts/dev/seed-prompts.ts BRB-019 Stop running api and web as root in development P3 closed 2026-08-28 (PR #406) defect no longer reproduces docker/api/Dockerfile:52 and docker/web/Dockerfile:23 run as USER ${DEV_UID}:${DEV_GID} (PR #406, closed before the finding was raised) BRB-020 Give every alert in brabo-alerts.yaml a severity P3 open defect no longer reproduces All five alerts carry severity: (deploy/k8s/observability/alerts/brabo-alerts.yaml:29,59,87,123,160). Not measured here: the "done when" also asks the operational dashboard to filter by it BRB-021 Fill the runbook gaps: rollout and cost incident P3 open defect no longer reproduces docs/runbook.md:1671 ## Engine rollout {#rollout-do-engine} and :2899 ## Cost incident {#incidente-de-custo}, both reached from the triage table (:21, :30) BRB-022 Fix the prose counts the repository already knew were wrong P2 closed 2026-09-27 (AT-136) defect no longer reproduces Closed by PR #530: CONTRIBUTING.md:11 (ADR count) is checked by pnpm docs:check, and the glossary's artifact-schema count is derived from Engine.Harness.ArtifactSchemas (scripts/docs/generate.mjs:623-624), exercised by mutation in both directions BRB-023 Update the vault: ADR 0127, RN-471/472 and the diverging ADR count P2 open not verifiable here The finding is about the vault's own notes. The repository can only give the numbers the vault should copy — docs/adr/ and the RN files are the source BRB-024 Remove references to folders and paths that no longer exist P3 open repository half no longer reproduces; vault half not verifiable here README.md:296 and docs/getting-started.md:274 say apps/api/src/db/schema/<aggregate>.ts, and both phrases are anchored to the code by verificarFrasesAncoradasNoCodigo; design_handoff_brabo/ appears only in historical prose. The notes the finding names (UX Designer, Local Development, Commands) live in the vault BRB-025 Include apps/api/scripts/ and e2e/ in the generated environment inventory P3 open defect no longer reproduces scripts/docs/fontes-de-env.mjs:49-52 scans both, and a new process.env.X there fails docs:check (AT-124, PR #638, measured by mutation). The half that stayed open — after docs:generate the ⚠️ did not fail, and HUGGINGFACE_API_TOKEN/HUGGINGFACE_HUB_URL were committed that way — closed in AT-211 (2026-09-27): docs:check fails on any ⚠️ in the environment inventory, both source kinds (scripts/docs/inventario-de-env.mjs, proven by mutation in inventario-de-env.spec.ts), and the two variables are described in configuration.md BRB-026 Reorganise docs/adr/index.md — everything since 0044 sits under "Phase 12" P3 open still reproduces docs/adr/index.md:143 ## Phase 12 — Post-dogfooding operability still holds every later ADR, and the index has no generated block BRB-027 Record the methodology behind the "Scale" table P3 open still reproduces There is no scripts/docs/escala.mjs and docs/architecture.md has no generated scale block; the table itself lives in the vault BRB-028 Give the appsec moment (threat_model) a trigger P2 closed 2026-09-27 (AT-136) defect no longer reproduces Was: SecOpsAgentServer.run_design/2 had no production caller, and docs/fluxo.yml named assess_implementability as the natural trigger while declaring it out of scope. Merged into dev by PR #514 (RN-539 — renumbered from 522, already taken two days earlier): dev_lead_tools.ex:333-338 fires it from assess_implementability, exactly where the gap said it belonged, through Dispatcher.run_appsec_design/2 (dispatcher.ex:112); docs/fluxo.yml:188-196 now reads status: active with no gap declared. The trigger is guarded by idempotence and that is not zeal: the :sem_plano outcome asks the model to call assess_implementability again, and each re-call would otherwise spend another appsec LLM round and three more handoffs on the same story. One limit stays declared in the code: artifact.threat_model is emitted in the STORY session while the guard reads the DEV LEAD session — the same session in the common path, and a repeated LLM round, never wrong data, when they differ BRB-029 Decide the fate of the Psychologist and Anamnesis (paused since 2026-08-10) P2 open not verifiable here — product decision The pause is declared as an open product decision in CLAUDE.md and became reversible with RN-540; no ADR records keeping it off for a set period BRB-030 Reconcile the duplicated tab navigation (rail × sidebar) P3 open not verifiable here — product decision CLAUDE.md lists the duplication (LinhaDeAba, RN-196) as an accepted gap and a separate product decision, not taken in ADR 0126 BRB-031 Remove the manual chmod +x from browser-driven runner setup P3 closed 2026-10-01 (AT-014) defect no longer reproduces Was: the File System Access API does not preserve the execute bit (docs/adr/0118-configuracao-automatica-do-runner-pelo-navegador.md:134-140), so the browser flow of ADR 0118 ended in a manual chmod +x. Half of it closed first by another path: install.sh places the binary with install -m 0755 (RN-531) and pairs the machine from the terminal (RN-547). The other half closed by the owner's decision (01/10) to retire the browser flow: ADR 0203 / RN-687 removed apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts and POST /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys, and RunnerOnboardingPanel now sends people to the installer command. grep -rn "chmod +x" apps/web/src finds only the panel docblock telling why the step left. Project keys registered by the browser before that keep working and stay revocable. The e2e download coverage the finding also asked for is moot: there is no browser download left to cover BRB-032 The broker never came up in the local compose P1 closed 2026-09-27 on the measured half only (AT-136) defect no longer reproduces on two of three halves; the third not exercised Closed in the vault on the measured half only. Measured: the broker left profiles: — the only profiles in the dev compose are local-llm (docker/docker-compose.yml:86,126); the root cause — corepack as root at build with no registry at runtime — was fixed by preparing COREPACK_HOME at build and adding a healthcheck (PR #503, RN-512), without giving the broker network; and .env.example no longer contradicts itself (2026-09-11). Still open: "container_start on a container project reaches the daemon" was never exercised — it needs an image decided by the Architect (RN-105), which no measured instance had BRB-033 reset-total.sh tore down the engine and the seed died with it P2 closed 2026-09-27 (AT-136) defect no longer reproduces 718b859e2 — "o reset total sobrevive a si mesmo e para de mentir no fim", merged into dev via c230e91af (PR #507). The script now probes /health of the three services and any failure exits naming the step On 2026-09-27 the vault records 10 closed (BRB-032 only on its measured half), 1 delivered and not yet marked closed (BRB-007) and 22 open. An open vault state next to "defect no longer reproduces" is not a contradiction: it is a closure the maintainer has not made yet.
documents.s: The register

documents.t: They are deliberately different words. Fixed would be the maintainer's judgement, recorded in the vault. Defect no longer reproduces is all this repository can honestly assert: the behaviour the finding describes is not what the code does today, measured at the date of the row. Implemented, not yet exercised is weaker: the code exists and the tests that can run do pass, but the path only executes somewhere this repository cannot reach — a real release tag, in CI. Calling that "fixed" would be claiming a proof nobody has. Still reproduces and partly reproduces say the finding's behaviour is still there, in whole or in part. Not verifiable here says the finding is about something this repository does not hold. Closing the item — and deciding whether the fix covers everything the finding asked for — stays where the finding was raised. BRB-004 is the reason the distinction earns its keep. Read from its id, it looked like the ollama:latest pin that closed in #419. Read from the vault, it asked for digests, which no image had. An id is not a description — and the misreading is what kept it open while a sibling rule for uses: had had a mechanism since #419.
documents.s: What the words in "measured here" mean

documents.t: The id, title and priority are copied from the vault verbatim, and so is the vault state; the "measured here" state and the evidence are measured here. A row changes when the vault changes its state or when a change in this repository changes what can be proved — never to invent a finding.
documents.s: Changing a row

documents.t: All configuration is via environment variable. There is no application config file — what exists is permissions.json, which is project policy, not process configuration. Two versioned files are read at runtime and are not configuration, although they're easy to confuse with it: permissions.json above, and docs/gates.yml (ADR 0054), the declarative gate registry. Neither has an environment variable to point to a path — the registry is found by walking up from __dirname — and neither changes behavior by being edited in production: the registry DESCRIBES the gates, it doesn't apply them. It travels inside the api image; see the runbook. What travels is the registry and nothing it points at. The evidencia of a teste/ci gate names files under apps/api/test/, scripts/ci/ and .github/, and none of those are in the image. Checking that those targets exist is therefore a claim about the repository, enforced in CI, never by the process serving GET /gates — which is why the api reads the registry without looking for them. It used to look, and it answered 500 in every installation (RN-070). up --wait only proves what has a healthcheck. In the development compose, api, engine and web had none, so docker compose up --wait reported them ready the moment the container started — before the process was listening. That is how a container could die seconds later with the command still reporting success. The three now carry the same check their production images already declare in the Dockerfile (/health for api and engine, which touches the database; / for the Vite server). The container broker got its own in a separate change; postgres and neo4j always had one. Nothing here is an environment variable — it is written down because --wait is the thing scripts trust, and a service without a healthcheck makes it lie. The defaults below were extracted from the code, not from prior documentation. The when it fails column is the part that saves time: almost every variable has a default that works in development and a specific failure mode in production. A variable only reaches the process if the compose maps it. docker compose does not forward the host environment into a container: a variable arrives if — and only if — it is written in that service's environment: (or an env_file). This is not a detail; it is how ANAMNESE_ENABLED and PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED stayed silently unreachable while three places in the code promised the 2026-08-10 pause was reversible with X=true plus a restart. Measured inside the running engine container, they came back empty and runtime.exs fell back to "false" — no error anywhere. Every boolean flag the engine reads is now mapped in all three compose files (dev, production and installation — the installation one only since AT-202), with the code's own default except for the two background-agent boot keys that production and installation turn off on purpose, and scripts/ci/flags-do-engine-no-compose.spec.ts fails the build for the next one that isn't (RN-540). Kubernetes is deliberately outside that rule: a Deployment/ConfigMap intercepts nothing, so there is no broken switch to fix there. Development defaults are insecure on purpose. Values like dev-master-key-change-me exist so pnpm dev comes up without ceremony. In production they need to be changed — and for six of them the process refuses to boot without changing them (api or engine, marked with 🔒). Five follow the pattern of ADR 0059/RN-093: missing, set to the public example literal, or too short brings the boot down. See RN-114 for the four that joined the original GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET.
documents.s: Configuration

documents.t: The compose that runs on an installed machine takes the five product images from mandatory variables, with no default — install.sh writes them into .env: variable what BRABO_API_IMAGE full reference of the api image; ghcr.io/…@sha256:… when the source is GHCR, brabo-api:prod when built locally BRABO_ENGINE_IMAGE same, for the engine BRABO_WEB_IMAGE same, for the web BRABO_BACKUP_IMAGE same, for the backup job (under the backup profile) BRABO_BROKER_IMAGE same, for the container broker (ADR 0162). Written whether or not the broker is turned on: Compose interpolates the whole file before filtering by profile, so a ${VAR:?…} on a disabled service still refuses the file (measured) They are ${VAR:?…} on purpose. With a default, a missing variable would bring half the stack up on an image nobody picked, and the mistake would show up as strange behaviour instead of a refusal. These are not in the generated inventory below: the generator scans apps/, and these are read by Compose, not by product code (RN-527). The broker is in this compose since ADR 0162, off, under the container-broker profile, and install.sh turns it on only when asked and answered "s" (RN-575). Then it writes four lines, together or not at all: variable what install.sh writes COMPOSE_PROFILES container-broker — read by Compose from the --env-file, so up -d --wait brings the broker up with no flag BROKER_URL http://broker:8090 — the api's side; without it the api never calls the broker DOCKER_GID the socket's gid as seen from inside a container, measured with the broker image itself; failing to measure is a named refusal, never the 999 default PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT <DockerRootDir>/volumes/brabo_project_workspaces/_data, computed before startup and checked against the volume's real Mountpoint after it BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE is not written: the compose derives it from BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, as in the validation compose. Turning it on or off later is in the runbook. The local models (Ollama, the llm profile) are asked about right after the broker (RN-691). Answering "s" measures a free host port first and writes: variable what install.sh writes OLLAMA_PORT 11434, or the first free port up to 11443 when something (a native Ollama) already listens there; the whole range busy is a named refusal, nothing written COMPOSE_PROFILES llm, joined with container-broker on ONE line when both were accepted (container-broker,llm) — two lines would not add up, the last one wins Without them the semantic duplicate check is skipped. Turning them on later is in the runbook.
documents.s: Installation compose (docker-compose.install.yml)

documents.t: variable default when it fails DATABASE_URL postgres://brabo:brabo@localhost:5432/brabo without it, nothing comes up PORT 3000 — API_JSON_BODY_LIMIT 10mb ceiling for the JSON body the api accepts, applied to the parser registered in main.ts before any route. It exists so that a change to the engine's transport ceiling (TRANSPORT_MAX_BODY_BYTES, 8 MiB) doesn't require a new deploy — the default keeps headroom over it. Too small, and a large context turn comes back as 413 NODE_ENV — production turns on strict CORS and key validation API_PUBLIC_URL http://localhost:3000 used in git OAuth callbacks; wrong = broken callback ENGINE_URL http://localhost:4000 in code, http://engine:4000 in Compose synchronous api→engine commands fail. Leave it empty in .env: set there, it wins over the Compose default and the api tries to talk to localhost:4000 from inside its own container — every session activation dies with ECONNREFUSED and the frontend never moves. Each environment already has the right default without the line ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL same as ENGINE_URL used only to build the engineWsUrl (WebSocket) returned in POST .../runner-ticket/.../terminal-ticket — the runner and the web can be OUTSIDE the cluster, so the internal address (http://engine:4000) doesn't work; ENGINE_URL remains the one used for the usual synchronous api→engine calls (RN-419) BRABO_VERSION dev becomes service.version in the OpenTelemetry resource — it's how you know which build generated a trace. The release image injects the tag via a docker-bake.hcl ARG; outside of a release it stays dev. It does not appear in /health, which deliberately doesn't return the version (see the route's description) MIGRATIONS_FOLDER ./src/db/migrations —
documents.s: Essentials

documents.t: variable default when it fails CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY 🔒 dev-master-key-change-me only outside production wraps the DEKs. In production the api refuses to boot if it's missing, set to the default above (public — it's in .env.example), or shorter than 16 characters (RN-114). This is only the BOOT check: swapping it for a valid but different key without re-wrapping still makes every credential unreadable with no error at all — the failure shows up on first use. See rotation CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY_PREVIOUS — only during rotation. Present = the api tries the previous key when the current one fails GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET 🔒 dev-oauth-state-secret-change-me only outside production signs the OAuth state; weak = CSRF in the git connection flow. In production the api refuses to boot without it, with the default above (which is public — it's in .env.example), or with fewer than 16 characters. Generate with openssl rand -base64 32. See ADR 0059 and RN-093 WEB_ORIGIN 🔒 http://localhost:${WEB_PORT} in production the api refuses to boot if it's missing or is *. CORS is strict per environment. The port is part of the value: the web on :5174 is a different origin and gets blocked — see ADR 0037. In the composes, the default derives from WEB_PORT, so changing the port carries CORS with it; setting WEB_ORIGIN by hand overrides the derivation and it becomes your responsibility to keep it consistent again WEB_PORT 5173 (dev) · 8088 (prod) published port of the web on the host. Not read by any service — it feeds the default of WEB_ORIGIN in the composes, and that's what keeps port and CORS from diverging
documents.s: Security 🔒

documents.t: Auth lives in the api's domain, and since the cutover it's also the sole issuer. Decisions in ADR 0031 and ADR 0032. variable default what it does AUTH_JWT_SECRET 🔒 dev-auth-jwt-secret-change-me only outside production passphrase the access token's Ed25519 pair is derived from via scrypt — no private key is committed. In production the api refuses to boot if it's missing, set to the default above (public — it's in .env.example), or shorter than 16 characters (RN-114) AUTH_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS — accepted only for verification, during rotation; enters the JWKS and never signs AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER 🔒 dev-auth-token-pepper-change-me only outside production HMAC key for hashing opaque tokens (refresh, account links, PATs) and the lockout bucket key. Its own secret — it no longer falls back to AUTH_JWT_SECRET (RN-613). In production the api refuses to boot if it's missing, set to either example value from this repository, or shorter than 16 characters. An installation that ran without it must set it to the current AUTH_JWT_SECRET, or everyone is logged out — see the runbook AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MS 900000 15 min AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_MS 1209600000 14 days AUTH_REFRESH_ABSOLUTE_TTL_MS 2592000000 absolute ceiling of the family, counted from login — without it rotation grants an eternal session AUTH_REGISTRATION_ENABLED true any value other than "false" keeps registration open AUTH_LOCKOUT_ENABLED true same convention AUTH_LOCKOUT_WINDOW_MS 900000 sliding window of the count AUTH_LOCKOUT_THRESHOLDS 5:30,8:300,12:900 email bucket ladder, failures:seconds AUTH_LOCKOUT_IP_THRESHOLDS 20:30,30:120 IP bucket ladder, more permissive and with a short ceiling AUTH_EMAIL_TOKEN_TTL_MS 172800000 email verification, 48 h AUTH_RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MS 3600000 password reset, 1 h AUTH_SET_PASSWORD_TTL_MS 604800000 setting the first password (migrated user), 7 days — longer than the reset because the recipient didn't ask for it AUTH_IP_ATTEMPT_THRESHOLD 60 ceiling of attempts per IP on the auth routes AUTH_MAIL_LOG_TOKENS false dev only: prints the verification/reset token to the log The email ladder's ceiling equals the window on purpose. With a sliding window, whoever keeps insisting pushes the window along and stays blocked for as long as they keep it up; whoever stopped comes back with a clean window. A ceiling larger than the window would create a lockout the window can't represent, and would require a persistent locked_until column with an unlock queue. Don't touch one without the other. Rotating AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER logs everyone out and invalidates outstanding verification and reset tokens. Unlike the keys, the pepper does not have a _PREVIOUS. See the runbook. Where the _PREVIOUS variables reach. AUTH_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS, CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY_PREVIOUS and BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN_PREVIOUS are mapped in the environment: of all three composes (dev, production and install) as ${X:-} — the api gets the three, the engine and the broker get BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN_PREVIOUS (RN-595). Empty is the same as absent in every reader, so outside a rotation nothing changes; during one, setting them in .env and recreating the service is enough. Before RN-595 they were mapped nowhere and docker compose doesn't forward the host environment, so a rotation silently became a hard swap. On Kubernetes they reach the Pods through the secret store (AT-220): the ExternalSecret pulls the whole brabo object with dataFrom.extract, so a _PREVIOUS present there lands in brabo-secrets and an absent one is simply not there. The price is that every key of that object becomes an environment variable of api, engine, migrations and backup — the store object must hold nothing else. The procedure is in the runbook.
documents.s: First-party auth

documents.t: MailSender sends real email only when MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp — the default is log (link/token go to the api's log, AUTH_MAIL_LOG_TOKENS above), including in production: sending email is the operator's opt-in. Decision in ADR 0096. variable default what it does MAIL_TRANSPORT log log (default) or smtp. Any other value falls back to log SMTP_HOST 🔒 — SMTP provider host. Only when MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp: in production the api refuses to boot if it's missing, whitespace-only, or set to the example value published in .env.example (RN-114) SMTP_PORT 587 provider port — 587 is STARTTLS, 465 is implicit TLS (SMTP_SECURE=true) SMTP_SECURE false true turns on implicit TLS on the connection (typically port 465) SMTP_USER 🔒 — SMTP auth username. Same requirement as SMTP_HOST in production SMTP_PASSWORD 🔒 — SMTP auth password/token. Same requirement as SMTP_HOST in production — never appears in logs SMTP_FROM — sender, format "Name <email@domain>" (or just the email). Same requirement as SMTP_HOST in production, plus format validation The email body is plain text, no HTML — the MailSender port doesn't carry structure for rich bodies, and a template engine would be an injection surface with no upside. The link uses WEB_ORIGIN (above).
documents.s: Real SMTP (MailSender)

documents.t: Consumed by pnpm --filter api seed, not by the running api. Without an external IdP, this is where the credential to log into the local web and the smoke test comes from. variable default what it does BRABO_SEED_PASSWORD brabo12345678 password of the seeded users (owner@brabo.dev, dev@brabo.dev), created with email already verified BRABO_FORCE_SEED — unlocks the seed with NODE_ENV=production, where it refuses to run by default. Do not set it in a real environment: the account is born with a known, verified password The seed is idempotent and doesn't touch the password of anyone who already exists. Running it again after someone has changed their own password doesn't revert it.
documents.s: Development seed

documents.t: Sliding window in Postgres — there's no Redis (ADR 0027). variable default what it does RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED true any value other than "false" keeps it on RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS 60000 window size RATE_LIMIT_USER 300 requests per user per window RATE_LIMIT_IP 600 requests per IP per window If the rate limit table is unavailable, the request goes through. The guard protects against abuse, not unauthorized access — that's the job of the authentication guard, which runs first.
documents.s: Rate limit

documents.t: The shared secret that authenticates api ↔ engine. The same variable on both sides — each one sends the current value and accepts both, and that's what makes rotation possible without downtime (RN-035). variable default what it does BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN 🔒 dev-service-token-change-me only outside production goes in the X-Brabo-Service-Token header and is what EngineServiceGuard compares in constant time. In production the api refuses to boot if it's missing, set to the default above (public — it's in .env.example), or shorter than 16 characters (RN-114) BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN_PREVIOUS — accepted only for verification, during rotation. When set, it goes through the same rule as the current token: surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and in production the api refuses to boot if it's the public default or shorter than 16 characters. Unlike the current token, it's never required (RN-598) Setting only the NEW value on one side (without going through the _PREVIOUS dance) doesn't break anyone's boot: the symptom is 403 on /internal/* and 401 on api-to-engine calls. Procedure in the runbook. The BOOT check above (RN-114) is a different thing: it only fails on the public default or a missing/short variable, not on a mismatch between the two sides.
documents.s: Internal traffic 🔒

documents.t: variable default note GIT_LOCAL_REPOS_ROOT /tmp/brabo-git-repos Local provider. In /tmp, repos disappear on reboot PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT /tmp/brabo-project-workspaces project agent worktrees in Container mode. Needs to be the same path on the engine, and the same volume BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE empty the single host folder under which Mounted-mode projects live, mounted by identity into api and engine. Empty is a NORMAL state: the api reports projectsBase: null and the project wizard doesn't offer Mounted mode at all GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET empty empty = GitHub OAuth connection unavailable (PAT still works) GITLAB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET empty same Project in Mounted mode: one base, mounted by identity​ Since ADR 0072, a project can be born in Mounted mode (the old local, renamed by ADR 0104) — the code lives in a user folder and PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT doesn't participate in its root. The path of a given project is a project-level datum (projects.workspace_path), chosen at creation and never an environment variable. What the ENVIRONMENT provides is the base those folders live under — BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, one per installation (ADR 0141, RN-500): # .env — ABSOLUTE. `~` is not expanded by Compose. BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE=/home/voce/projetos-brabo You don't have to write that line by hand. Since ADR 0146, pnpm bootstrap → Docker › Base de projetos runs scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs, which proposes $HOME/projetos-brabo, refuses anything overlapping either the Brabo checkout or PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR (two roots with opposite owners — sharing a folder would make a Mounted project called loja land on top of a Container project whose workspace_dir_name is also loja), proves on macOS and Windows that Docker can actually see the folder by mounting it, and only then writes the variable. The proof is a mount, never a read of Docker Desktop's settings.json: that file is undocumented, differs across versions and platforms, and describes what the user configured rather than what the daemon will do — the same rule the product already applies to LLM providers, where a capability is declared only when proved by execution. It has three outcomes and they don't collapse: proved, refused (the variable is not written), and couldn't prove — no local image to mount with — which writes the variable and says loudly that the proof did not run. Run from the menu it only reports: every bootstrap menu item runs with stdin from /dev/null on purpose, so it cannot ask. To choose, run node scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs in your own terminal. # docker/docker-compose.yml — on BOTH `api` and `engine`, already written volumes: - ${BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE:-brabo_projects_base}:${BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE:-/data/brabo-projects-base} The operator sets this once and restarts api + engine; nothing is edited per project, ever. Before this, every mounted project needed a hand-written bind-mount line in both services plus a restart — which kills every in-flight agent turn, terminal socket and LLM call in the installation. The mount is by identity ($X:$X): the same absolute path on the host and inside both containers. That is what keeps honest the string the user types and the screen shows back, and it is why projectScopeRoot (api) and Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/2 (engine) need no translation layer. It is not PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR, and must never point at the same folder. A managed workspace is named by workspace_dir_name (UNIQUE) and a mounted project is named by the user, so <base>/loja and a container project whose folder name is loja would collide, with the repo bootstrap running git init inside someone else's project. The ADR has the other two reasons. With the variable unset, Mounted mode isn't offered — never offer a mode the installation can't honor. And pnpm dev refuses to start when the base overlaps the Brabo checkout in either direction; that check lives in the preflight because it runs on the host, and the api can only compare against process.cwd() (/workspace inside its own container). See the runbook.
documents.s: Git

documents.t: variable default note OLLAMA_HOST http://localhost:11434 — OLLAMA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 300000 inactivity ceiling of the Ollama socket, not total duration. A local model has a different order of magnitude of latency to the first token, hence its own env var; see inference environment LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 300000 the same inactivity ceiling for the API providers (OpenAI and compatible, Anthropic). Applies to "didn't even send the headers" and to "stopped sending chunks mid-stream" — see LLM providers HUGGINGFACE_API_TOKEN (unset) optional Hugging Face Hub token for the model search (GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/huggingface/models). Present, it goes as Authorization: Bearer … and raises the Hub's rate limit; absent, the header is simply not sent — the Hub accepts public search without a credential, and a missing token is never an error HUGGINGFACE_HUB_URL https://huggingface.co base URL of the Hub the search talks to. An override for tests (a fake HTTP server on an ephemeral port); in production it is left unset HUGGINGFACE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 15000 inactivity ceiling of the Hub search request, same semantics as LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (the name is built in a constant, so the generated inventory below does not see it) TODO(humano): no compose file maps the three HUGGINGFACE_* variables into the api service's environment:, and the service has no env_file, so setting them in the .env has no effect under Compose — should HUGGINGFACE_API_TOKEN be forwarded (at least in production and installation)?
documents.s: LLM

documents.t: variable default note NEO4J_URI — e.g. bolt://neo4j:7687. This one is the switch: empty = graph OFF, dependent routes degrade (GraphUnavailableError/503) — nobody needs a local Neo4j just to run the suite. In production, the absence of any of the three brings the boot down. Turning the graph on in development is this one line in .env and a restart of the api; until 2026-09-04 that did nothing, because the dev compose did not pass the three variables to the api service at all and the service has no env_file — docker-compose.prod.yml had supplied them since day one, which is why only development was affected NEO4J_USER neo4j (dev) reaches the container with the same default the neo4j service uses for NEO4J_AUTH, so set it only to CHANGE the user — changing it there changes both sides at once. Two independent defaults would leave the api authenticating with credentials the server no longer has NEO4J_PASSWORD 🔒 dev-neo4j-password-change-me (dev only) same pairing rule as NEO4J_USER. No public default in production on purpose — there's no plausible "example value" for a database password, and docker-compose.prod.yml keeps NEO4J_AUTH empty so the official image's own entrypoint refuses to start rather than booting with a guessable one GRAPH_PROJECTOR_INTERVAL_MS 2000 period of the poller that drains the outbox's graph_projection queue and writes handoffs/hypotheses/profiles/interactions to the graph (RN-416) ARTIFACT_PROJECTOR_INTERVAL_MS 2000 period of the poller that drains the outbox's artifact_projection queue and writes each agent's artifacts as Markdown under the project's docs/ folder (RN-523). A DERIVED projection: the event log stays the source, and the folder can be deleted and rebuilt
documents.s: Knowledge graph (ADR 0099)

documents.t: variable default note OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT — missing turns off EXPORT, not instrumentation (ADR 0035). The span is still created and trace_id still shows up in the log — that's what gives correlation in development, without a collector. Without it, the span is discarded at the end instead of leaving the process OTEL_SERVICE_NAME brabo-api — OTEL_DIAG_LOG — 1 turns on OTel's own diagnostic log LOG_LEVEL info in production, debug outside also decides the FORMAT together with NODE_ENV: outside production the log comes out readable (pino-pretty in-process, with the layer tree); in production, one JSON line per event METRICS_GAUGE_INTERVAL_MS 15000 collection period of the domain gauges
documents.s: Observability
